example.sql:
-- The five players with the most shot attempts, most first.
SELECT player_name, team_name, attempts
FROM bb_shots
ORDER BY attempts DESC
LIMIT 5

exercises.prompt: List the 11 players with the most shot attempts: player_name, team_name and attempts, in that order, most attempts first. Two players can have the same number of attempts, so break ties by player_name, from A to Z.
hints: ORDER BY takes several columns: the second one only decides between rows that tie on the first.
DESC sorts from the largest down; a column without it sorts up (A to Z for text).
LIMIT 11 keeps the first 11 rows of the sorted result.
exercises.solution:
SELECT player_name, team_name, attempts
FROM bb_shots
ORDER BY attempts DESC, player_name
LIMIT 11

exercises.prompt: Which five players scored the most points? Return player_name and total_points, in that order. The order of the rows does not matter here: the checker compares them as a set.
hints: The rows can come in any order, but picking the top five still needs ORDER BY.
Sort by total_points from the largest down, then keep five rows with LIMIT.
exercises.solution:
SELECT player_name, total_points
FROM bb_shots
ORDER BY total_points DESC
LIMIT 5
